assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues turned the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical tool, giving a new modality that can reach proteins previously considered undruggable. It is a clear case of molecular design principles reshaping what chemists and clinicians can do, with wide uptake in chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) made the original PROTAC concept; Ciulli supplied the structure-guided VHL ligands that made degraders drug-like. Handa, Ito and Kim relate to the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, a separate but related strand. The three-person split is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Several degraders are in advanced clinical trials, and the field has been independently reproduced at large scale. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is still pending, so some may see recognition as slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should credit PROTACs and molecular glues together, which would force a different allocation of credit.
Sakamoto, Handa and Ito have strong claims, so the three-name limit leaves out important contributors.
Final clinical validation is not yet complete (from my own knowledge, not independently verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, fusing deaminase chemistry with programmable CRISPR targeting. The concept was original, it was demonstrated clearly, and it spread to basic research and therapeutic programmes, including clinical use.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led both cytosine and adenine base editor development, and Komor and Gaudelli did the key work as trainees in his lab. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase editor, so credit has some overlap, but Liu is the clear intellectual driver.
assessment.maturity: Replication is wide, and clinical reports of base-edited therapies have appeared. A chemistry prize is plausible since CRISPR was already recognised in 2020, though the question is how soon after that.
uncertainties: Overlap with the separate prime-editing entry B046, which could be recognised together with this one.
Whether the committee wants to honour a second genome-editing prize so soon after 2020.
Long-term clinical safety data are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing is a transformational analytical technology, with sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and single-molecule/array-based readout. It reshaped biology and clinical diagnostics and made genomes routine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa reversible-terminator chemistry and clustering concept; Rothberg led the parallel pyrosequencing (454) platform. Ju and Mayer have relevant, but more specialised, claims. The credit configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Impact has been demonstrated for roughly two decades, so recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Competing claims between the Solexa and 454 lineages and other contributors.
The work may be considered more a technology and biology prize than a molecular-chemistry one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a molecularly designed delivery system, with pKa tuning for encapsulation and endosomal release, that enabled siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines. The societal impact is very large and the chemistry is a clear design story.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) made the foundational lipid and formulation advances; Anderson and Langer made combinatorial lipid design and delivery advances. Credit is distributed across several teams and I am unsure which of them are decisive.
assessment.maturity: The technology is validated by approved siRNA and mRNA products. The 2023 Medicine Nobel for mRNA modification may shape how the committee sees timing and overlap.
uncertainties: Hard to isolate decisive contributors among many industry and academic groups.
Possible overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may reduce appetite for it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs lets researchers site-specifically encode non-canonical amino acids in living cells. It gives precise chemical control over proteins and has been adopted widely in chemical biology and protein therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal-pair approach in E. coli and then eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding and animals; Wang made early contributions in cells and with Schultz. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed. The split is reasonable but not exclusive.
assessment.maturity: It has been applied and reproduced for more than two decades and its use in biologics is increasing.
uncertainties: Several credit claims are hard to rank.
Impact on drug development is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids gave rational, sequence-controlled design of nanomaterials and became a platform for biosensing, intracellular gene regulation and diagnostics. This is close to my own field of nanoparticle biosensing, and the design principle is clear.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently published DNA-nanoparticle assembly in 1996, and Mirkin then developed the spherical nucleic acid concept and its applications. Storhoff and Mucic were key co-authors, but a two-person prize would reflect the founding papers.
assessment.maturity: The assembly work is well confirmed. Clinical translation of spherical nucleic acids is still partial.
uncertainties: Priority overlap between Mirkin and Alivisatos, and Alivisatos is better known for quantum dots.
Therapeutic and commercial impact is still limited compared with the strongest candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules through nanopores gave a new sensing modality and the first portable long-read sequencers, and it is a clear molecular engineering success based on protein pores and ionic-current analysis.
assessment.attribution: Bayley developed protein-pore engineering and sensing; Akeson and Deamer demonstrated DNA translocation and enzyme-controlled movement; Kasianowicz and Branton did the earliest pore work. The credit is tangled across several decisive contributions, so the list is a choice among strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices have been in use for years and the methods are well replicated, with an increasingly broad range of applications.
uncertainties: Complex priority history among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Akeson and Bayley.
May be considered together with next-generation sequencing, so the committee could decide on only one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses covalent chemical probes to read out enzyme function directly in complex proteomes, and it supports target discovery and covalent drug design. It is a chemical tool that changed how researchers can query biology and develop drugs.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the central figure for the proteome-wide platform and its application; Bogyo and Overkleeft built key probe classes, especially for proteases and the proteasome. The roles are clear, and Weerapana is less likely to be a laureate.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established and widely reproduced, including in clinical covalent-ligand development.
uncertainties: Reading the history of early probe design (for example Cravatt versus Bogyo/Overkleeft and earlier work) may lead to different attribution.
Whether committee members see this as a tool prize or as a prize of broad enough significance.
